topicName: Deploying MongoDB on GCP (Compute Engine, Persistent Disks, VPC)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Deploying MongoDB on GCP (Compute Engine, Persistent Disks, VPC)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial outlines the steps to deploy MongoDB on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) using Compute Engine, Persistent Disks, and Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). This setup provides a robust and scalable environment for your MongoDB database."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A Google Cloud Platform (GCP) account with billing enabled."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic understanding of GCP services like Compute Engine, Persistent Disks, and VPC."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Familiarity with Linux command-line interface."},{"order":7,"type":"heading","text":"Step 1: Create a VPC Network"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"A VPC network enables you to control the network configuration for your Compute Engine instances. Create a new VPC network or use an existing one."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute networks create mongodb-vpc --subnet-mode=auto"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"This command creates a VPC named 'mongodb-vpc' with auto subnet creation. Auto subnet mode automatically creates a subnet in each region."},{"order":11,"type":"heading","text":"Step 2: Create a Compute Engine Instance"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a Compute Engine instance within the VPC network. Choose an appropriate machine type based on your workload requirements."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute instances create mongodb-instance --zone=us-central1-a --machine-type=e2-medium --image-family=debian-10 --image-project=debian-cloud --network-interface subnet=mongodb-vpc"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"This command creates an instance named 'mongodb-instance' in the 'us-central1-a' zone, using a Debian 10 image and attaching it to the 'mongodb-vpc' network."},{"order":15,"type":"heading","text":"Step 3: Create and Attach a Persistent Disk"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Persistent disks provide durable storage for your MongoDB data. Create a persistent disk and attach it to the Compute Engine instance."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute disks create mongodb-data-disk --size=100GB --zone=us-central1-a"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute instances attach-disk mongodb-instance --disk=mongodb-data-disk --device-name=mongodb-data --zone=us-central1-a"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"These commands create a 100GB persistent disk named 'mongodb-data-disk' and attach it to the 'mongodb-instance' as 'mongodb-data'."},{"order":20,"type":"heading","text":"Step 4: Connect to the Instance and Prepare the Disk"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"SSH into the Compute Engine instance and format and mount the persistent disk."},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute ssh mongodb-instance --zone=us-central1-a"},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"sudo mkfs.ext4 -m 0 -F /dev/sdb"},{"order":24,"type":"code","text":"sudo mkdir /data/db"},{"order":25,"type":"code","text":"sudo mount /dev/sdb /data/db"},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"sudo chown mongodb:mongodb /data/db"},{"order":27,"type":"code","text":"sudo echo '/dev/sdb /data/db ext4 defaults,nofail 0 2' | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab"},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"These commands format the disk, create a mount point, mount the disk, change ownership, and add an entry to /etc/fstab to ensure the disk is mounted on boot."},{"order":29,"type":"heading","text":"Step 5: Install MongoDB"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"Install MongoDB on the Compute Engine instance. Follow the official MongoDB installation guide for your chosen Linux distribution."},{"order":31,"type":"code","text":"wget -qO - https://www.mongodb.org/static/pgp/server-4.4.asc | sudo apt-key add -"},{"order":32,"type":"code","text":"echo "deb [ arch=amd64,arm64 ] https://repo.mongodb.org/apt/debian buster/mongodb-org/4.4 main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/mongodb-org-4.4.list"},{"order":33,"type":"code","text":"sudo apt-get update"},{"order":34,"type":"code","text":"sudo apt-get install -y mongodb-org"},{"order":35,"type":"paragraph","text":"These commands add the MongoDB repository, update the package list, and install MongoDB."},{"order":36,"type":"heading","text":"Step 6: Configure MongoDB"},{"order":37,"type":"paragraph","text":"Configure MongoDB to use the persistent disk for data storage. Edit the MongoDB configuration file (/etc/mongod.conf)."},{"order":38,"type":"code","text":"sudo nano /etc/mongod.conf"},{"order":39,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modify the 'dbPath' setting to point to the mounted persistent disk:"},{"order":40,"type":"code","text":"storage:
  dbPath: /data/db"},{"order":41,"type":"paragraph","text":"Optionally, configure network settings to restrict access to the MongoDB instance.  Consider setting 'bindIp' to '127.0.0.1' for local access only, or to a specific internal IP address for access from other instances within the VPC."},{"order":42,"type":"code","text":"net:
  port: 27017
  bindIp: 127.0.0.1"},{"order":43,"type":"heading","text":"Step 7: Start MongoDB"},{"order":44,"type":"paragraph","text":"Start the MongoDB service."},{"order":45,"type":"code","text":"sudo systemctl start mongod"},{"order":46,"type":"code","text":"sudo systemctl enable mongod"},{"order":47,"type":"paragraph","text":"These commands start the MongoDB service and enable it to start automatically on boot."},{"order":48,"type":"heading","text":"Step 8: Verify MongoDB Installation"},{"order":49,"type":"paragraph","text":"Verify that MongoDB is running correctly."},{"order":50,"type":"code","text":"sudo systemctl status mongod"},{"order":51,"type":"code","text":"mongo"},{"order":52,"type":"paragraph","text":"The 'mongo' command will open the MongoDB shell, allowing you to interact with the database."},{"order":53,"type":"heading","text":"Step 9: Configure Firewall Rules (Optional)"},{"order":54,"type":"paragraph","text":"If you need to access MongoDB from outside the Compute Engine instance (e.g., from another instance in the VPC or from your local machine), you need to configure firewall rules to allow traffic on port 27017."},{"order":55,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-mongodb --allow tcp:27017 --source-ranges=0.0.0.0/0 --network=mongodb-vpc"},{"order":56,"type":"paragraph","text":"Warning: Opening the firewall to 0.0.0.0/0 allows access from any IP address. For production environments, restrict the source ranges to only trusted IP addresses or networks."},{"order":57,"type":"heading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":58,"type":"paragraph","text":"You have successfully deployed MongoDB on GCP using Compute Engine, Persistent Disks, and VPC. This setup provides a scalable and reliable environment for your MongoDB database. Remember to secure your MongoDB instance by configuring authentication and authorization."}]
